title: Never too LATE: Exploiting restrictions for inference on the Local Average Treatment Effect
abstract: arXiv:2611.21496v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Under the exclusion restriction, independence, and monotonicity assumptions, Imbens and Angrist (1994) show that the Wald estimand is equal to the local average treatment effect (LATE). However, these assumptions entail additional restrictions, which we exploit for inference on the LATE. Specifically, we propose a conditional likelihood ratio test that we show controls asymptotic size uniformly over a large class of data-generating processes. The test has very low computational cost: it requires no simulation and involves solving at most four quadratic programming problems. Monte Carlo simulations show that our test can offer substantial power gains over the Wald and Anderson-Rubin tests, including when the instrument is weak.

translated_title: 永不嫌迟：利用约束条件对局部平均处理效应进行推断
translated_abstract: 在排除性约束、独立性和单调性假设下，Imbens和Angrist（1994）证明Wald估计量等于局部平均处理效应（LATE）。然而，这些假设蕴含了额外的约束条件，我们利用这些约束对LATE进行推断。具体而言，我们提出了一个条件似然比检验，并证明该检验在一大类数据生成过程上一致地控制了渐近检验水平。该检验的计算成本极低：它不需要模拟，且最多只需求解四个二次规划问题。蒙特卡洛模拟表明，与Wald检验和Anderson-Rubin检验相比，我们的检验可以带来显著的检验功效提升，即使在工具变量较弱的情况下也是如此。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种计算成本极低的条件似然比检验方法，通过利用LATE识别假设所蕴含的额外约束条件，实现对局部平均处理效应的有效推断，其检验功效显著优于Wald检验和Anderson-Rubin检验，即使在弱工具变量情形下也依然稳健。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a computationally cheap conditional likelihood ratio test for the LATE that exploits additional restrictions implied by standard identification assumptions, uniformly controlling asymptotic size and delivering substantial power gains over the Wald and Anderson-Rubin tests, even under weak instruments.
